root.Text: Spawn Butterflies: spawn a cluster of lovely, distracting butterflies! \n The island's butterflies remind villagers of life's beauty, \n drawing people together.

Swarm of Bees: spawn a bunch of stinging bees! 
 The island's pollinators promote growth and vigilance. 
 Both helpful and harmful, they must be respected, 
 like all things on Isola.
Sunshine: make it sunny. The island's light shines in places \n obscured by darkness. It serves to brighten spirits \n and drive away sadness.
Lightning Strike: a bolt of lightning from above! \n The island's tension manifests into focused energy, \n signalling places where renewal and restoration are most needed.
Hand of Bloom: spontaneous vegetative growth. The island \n nourishes all who live in harmony with its magic.
Tempest: summon a grand storm! The island's sorrow cries out \n to the heavens, bringing forth cleansing, renewal and healing in its wake.
Earthquake: shake the very island itself! The island rumbles \n with renewed strength and vigor, reminding all to listen closely to its call.
Fog of Doom: a fog so thick that visibility is crippled. \n The island conceals the physical and the divine, allowing people to see \n what remains hidden in the heart.
Time Warp: accelerate time for one islander. The island \n grants adaptability and wisdom as gifts to improve others' lives.
Grant Youth: make someone (quite) young again. The island \n offers second chances, allowing villagers to rise both wiser and stronger.
Revive: bring a fallen tribe member back! The island breathes \n life where loss once lingered, restoring balance and hope to its people.

There was once a mysterious island called Isola,\n
home to a tribe of lost refugees.\n
One day a child made a discovery.\n
on a forbidden path, at the edge of the village.\n
The elders gathered to examine the mask.\n They had never seen one like it before.\n

They must determine if others are nearby, so they appoint 
 a small group of villagers to search the forbidden path.
Note: If you have not played this mod before, I highly recommend clicking everything
and playing the Tutorial to see what's changed in the text and graphics. - Lorsieab2
The path took them into the darkest parts of the jungle.\n
Although they could see no one, they sensed they were being watched.\n
Your villagers have been captured and are now the prisoners of this mysterious tribe!\n
Do you need help getting started?\n
On this day the new believer told his sad story.\n
"Long ago there was a war between two factions in the island.\n
The conflict began with a forbidden love...\n
but ended with bloodshed and destruction."\n
"Those who survived the battle fled into the night.\n
"We retreated into the jungle and into a despair so deep and suffocating that we lost all hope.\n
We stopped believing in the island, in any guiding force. We even stopped believing in ourselves, \n
and so we covered our faces with these masks to protect us. We vowed to never forget \n
the horrors we endured, and to carry on the memory of those who perished.\n
"Your kindness, your words and actions, have reminded me that life is wonderful and worth living.\n
The others still live in fear and sorrow, as I once did. We must help them see \n
the goodness in people, without forgetting the sacrifices of the past.\n
I will keep this mask here with me to commemorate those we lost and to remind myself of \n
the trials I worked so hard to overcome. Our chief... he had a daughter..."\n
"I loved my daughter. I had forgotten that love.\n
I thought I could never love again. I've longed to see her all this time.\n
Seeing this necklace again has reminded me of how much she loved life, and all things in this world." \n
The Chief realizes his daughter would not have wanted him to live shut off from the world. \n With a trembling hand, he reaches out, at last opening his heart to the kindness around him. \n
\n "Thank you, everyone, for all you've done. Our ancestors have truly blessed us all this time." \n
\n After overcoming many challenges, all tribes of Isola now unite as one. \n
\n The lost have found hope, and the sorrowful can finally let go of their pain. Harmony has returned to Isola! \n

Let's explore the area...
 Click and hold the mouse button 
 anywhere on the ground and drag the 
 mouse to move around the village.

Good! This is how you move about 
 the island. Feel free to explore your
 little village.

Let's get to know one of the villagers...
 Find and click a villager, one without a mask, 
 to select them.

Perfect! A white circle shows which 
 villager is selected. See important 
 details about this villager, like their 
 name, at the bottom of the screen.

Let's move a villager...
 Click and hold the mouse button 
 on a villager and drag the mouse 
 to move them.

Excellent! Moving villagers influences their 
 behavior. Drag and drop villagers anywhere 
 you like to help them explore useful or 
 interesting places in the village.

Your villagers interact with many 
 locations around the map. Let's 
 start by dragging one of them to the green 
 bamboo fence that imprisons them.

Your villagers are using the green bamboo 
 to build a bin to store much-needed food. 
 Keep your villagers working on it.

You will notice there are villagers 
 wearing various colorful masks. 
 Find and click a villager wearing a blue mask.

You selected a member of the Native Isola Tribe. 
 They seem to be despondent and are untrusting of strangers, so 
 you cannot check their details or interfere with them. 
 Villagers wearing blue masks are not aggressive.
Find and click a villager wearing an orange mask.\n

You selected an Isolan warrior. 
 Isolan warriors will protect their people at all costs. 
 If they see a stranger from another tribe, they will chase them away.
Find and click a villager wearing a red mask.\n

You selected a senior Isolan warrior. 
 They are the highest-ranked warriors in their tribe, and their masks are imbued with protective magic. 
 When strangers look at them, they will be magically repelled by an invisible barrier. This causes them to run away. 
 This helps keep their people and territory safe from outsiders, but also isolates them in a way.
Try dropping one of your villagers onto \n a villager wearing a blue mask. \n

Good! The two villagers are finding common ground 
 and beginning to understand one another. At first, both your tribe and the Native Isolans will have 
 little knowledge of the other's culture, leading to superstition and mistrust. As they spend more time speaking, the more insight they will gain about shared values and practices. Over time, their tribes will learn how to treat each other with dignity, which is crucial for building trust and forming alliances.
 When the villager's Trust meter crosses the middle, he or she will 
 become allied with your tribe.

Villagers who are allied with you increase the island's 
 Life Energy. Life Energy is a measure of peace and balance on Isola, 
 which strengthens its Magic Powers. Isola responds to the world and its people. 
 Its magic is mysterious and beautiful - but also unpredictable. 
 When the island unleashes its magic, villagers can respond in various ways. 
 Let's try a Power now and spawn some butterflies. 
 Click the butterfly icon on the top left of the screen, 
 then click somewhere to release them.

Wow! Butterflies are great for distracting 
 children of all kinds. 
 Notice how you used a little bit of Life Energy. 
 The more villagers that trust your tribe, the faster the 
 energy will replenish.

Let's teach one of your villagers to research...
 Drag an adult villager to the large 
 table at the center of the lab.

Oh no! Your villager is being chased away! 
 The Native Isolans have settled this place for many centuries 
 and have great fear of strangers. From the looks of things, 
 they appear to have gone through a lot of hardship.
 In order to gain tech points, you will need 
 to help the Isolans restore their village by working together. 
 Once you renovate the research area, the tribe can start 
 generating tech points.

Let's check out the Technologies screen...
 Click the 'Tech' button on the left side of 
 the screen.

Welcome to the Technologies screen. 
 Use the tech points gained from research 
 to upgrade a variety of different technologies. 
 The right side of the screen shows all the powers 
 you have unlocked, as well as those you have not yet unlocked. 
 They can be unlocked by increasing Isola's Life Energy. 
 Click 'Done' to return to the main screen.

Children can also contribute to village life. 
 Their keen eyes can spot mushrooms and small 
 collectibles that adults might overlook. 
 Drag a child to this collectible before it disappears.

Ooooh! The child found a relic! 
 Your villagers can collect Isola's small and 
 beautiful treasures, but only when found by 
 a child. Repeat relics are converted into 
 Life Energy, while repeat lab gear gets converted into tech points.

Let's check out the Collections screen. 
 Click the 'Collections' button on the left 
 side of the screen.

Welcome to the Collections screen. 
 Here you can see which collectibles your 
 village children have gathered. Each relic that 
 you collect permanently increases the maximum 
 Life Energy level. Each piece of lab gear permanently 
 increases tech point production! 
 Click 'Done' to return to the main screen.

Let's learn more about a villager...
 Click the 'Detail' button at the 
 bottom of the screen.

Welcome to the Villager Detail screen. 
 Learn more about each villager, such 
 as trust, health and skills. Check the 
 box to the right of a skill to set a 
 skill preference. Click 'Done' to return 
 to the main screen.

You can see the status of the game's puzzles on the Puzzles and Milestones screen. 
 Click the 'Puzzles' button on the left 
 side of the screen.

Welcome to the Puzzles and Milestones screen. 
 The island is full of puzzles and hidden secrets 
 waiting to be discovered. Your goal is to solve 
 Isola's puzzles while helping your tribe 
 survive and make more new believers.

Well, as we approach the conclusion of this tutorial, 
 we arrive at the inevitable topic of making babies! 
 Deploy builders on the love shack to provide a romantic 
 place to get together. Take your time... When you manage 
 to get it finished, the final steps of the tutorial will resume.

Good!
 The love shack is a romantic hut and a perfect place 
 for village couples to discuss starting or adding to 
 their families and the tribe!

Let's make some babies...
 Drag an adult male villager onto an 
 adult female villager or vice versa. 
 A villager will not seek a mate on 
 their own unless they are trained and 
 Parenting is set as their preferred skill.

Good! They get along and want to 
 go indoors for some privacy. With any 
 luck, the stork may bring a new baby.

I'm sorry. One of your little villagers is dead. 
 Villagers die of old age, but they can also die 
 from disease and starvation. Buying medicine 
 technology helps your villagers live longer

Welcome to the Overview Map. 
 Enjoy a bird's-eye view of your village, 
 then click anywhere on the map to zoom 
 in to that spot.

Virtual Villagers is a true real-time game. 
 Your tribe continues to do what they have learned, 
 even when the computer is off or you stop playing, 
 but remember to check back often to care for 
 your little villagers! Have fun!

You have mastered the basics! 
 How you manage your tribe now is up to you! 
 Decide wisely who will do what. Your villagers 
 will slowly learn to do the tasks you show them. 
 Once survival is no longer an issue, you can 
 help them uncover the hidden secrets of Isola!

Hmmm... This villager is confused. 
 Sometimes villagers need more skill 
 or more advanced technology before

Great! You set a villager's skill preference. 
 From now on, they prefer this type of work 
 and gain skill the more they practice.

Nice try, but children don't work. They 
 love to play and won't do what you ask

 out though, as they sometimes find 
 delicious mushrooms or collectibles.
Parents don't work while they \n are caring for an infant. \n
Good. Let's watch this villager make a supply \n of cutting tools for the tribe. \n

Congratulations! One of your villagers 
 reached the `Trainee` level in a skill

Good job! Your villagers aren't worried about

One of the young children of your tribe is now 
 old enough to work! Your tribe needs every 
 able-bodied person to help out, so find that 
 villager, give them a job and keep everyone productive.
You cannot touch this villager because they wish to be left alone.\n \n
You cannot view details about this villager. They don't trust you yet.\n \n

You befriended someone and helped them in their time of need! Any time you increase your tribe's population, \n through conversation or new babies, you increase Isola's Life Energy, \n which can eventually unlock new powers!
Some totems will require magic powers to help your villagers \n fix them. If you are stuck, work on increasing population \n and collecting relics.
Recovering relics adds to Isola's Life Energy, \n which can unlock new, exciting powers!
Assigning builders to polish the statue helps them to \n practice building and gives the island a bit of energy each time!
You can only try to talk to the Native Isolans once, then you must wait a while before you can try again. \n The glowy light above them means they are tired of listening for now!
You have a new power! As you increase the number of \n people who are allied with you, new powers become available.

One of your villagers is a master in a skill! 
 This is a great accomplishment. Making any one 
 villager a master in at least three skills grants 
 that villager the prestigious title of Esteemed Elder.
Congratulations! Your village reached its \n first population milestone of 15 people!\n
Congratulations! Your village reached its \n second population milestone of 25 people!\n
Congratulations! Your village reached its \n third population milestone of 50 people!\n
Congratulations! Your village reached \n its maximum sustainable population!\n
Your villagers found an interesting new\n recipe!\n

Alas, the fates were not kind to your village. 
 All of your little villagers died. The island 
 of Isola remains a myth and its mysteries 
 unsolved.

 who has now allied with the tribe!

The Heartbroken Chief
 
 Your villagers have helped give the 
 heartbroken Chief a new lease on life!

A Family Reunited
 
 The tribes of Isola have now fully united in friendship. 
 They now gather as one family, ready to face the future together. 
 As Isola's Guardians of Harmony, the villagers will forever be

The Tribute Statue

The Protective Parent

 This will help them raise smarter

The Troubled Scientist

The Despondent Builder

 of the despondent builder!

The Despairing Farmer

 advanced hydroponic farm,

A New Hut!

The Clothing Hut

The Love Shack

Fire!

The Lake

Relic Collection

One morning, the villagers noticed that the beach looked very wrong. The waves had ceased their normal rhythm, and the water had receded so far that it almost looked as though the ocean itself was drying up. Their apprehension became alarm as a powerful tsunami crashed down upon the village, obliterating structures, and, sadly, sweeping many villagers to a watery end.

One morning, the villagers noticed that there was an aggressive and toxic mold spreading inside the food bin and ruining the contents. The frantic villagers do their best to save the food, but they can't save it all...
It's springtime, and all the flowers are in bloom. Many of the villagers suffer a temporary bout of hay fever.
Today is the day that the villagers commemorate their arrival on the island of Isola with dancing, celebration and feasts!
Today is the first day of the rainy season, marked by the first afternoon monsoon. Wow! It's really coming down!
An unseasonably cold, wet wind has blown through the village. The villagers were going to huddle around the fire, but the wet, icy drizzle put it out!
Army ants came and devoured the crops!
Aphids have infested the crops and rendered much of the food unusable.
Some very unusual green crystals have been found near a cave where lightning struck. The scientists can definitely use this. \n Your tribe gains tech points.

The Native Isolans often experiment with magic and technology in the lab, and unpredictable things happen as a side effect. During one such experiment, one of the apprentices makes a mistake and accidentally creates the most truly offensive, foul, and utterly eye-watering cloud of lingering gas to ever assault a nose! The lab, and soon the entire village, is quickly evacuated as dozens of villagers flee in panic covering their noses and mouths. The scientists manage to fully decontaminate the area, determining no further threat to health and safety. The apprentice's pride may have been injured a bit, but no harm or hard feelings have been made. The unfortunate incident quickly becomes a cautionary tale as well as a humorous memory for the ages.

One day, one of the villagers responsible for a lot of the cooking finds a small bottle full of red juice. It smells like herbs, so the villager puts it into the food. Everyone is shocked by the meal, which burns their mouths! Later on, everyone seems to need to relieve themselves at the same time!
There was a big rainstorm overnight that caused the stream to overflow its banks. It made a bit of a mess, but it deposited rich, fertile silt over all the crops. It should help them grow.

One of the Native Isolans brings a vial to show their fellow tribe members by the noni bush. They explain that it's a new potion they've developed, and proudly pours it on the ground. A few days later, the noni bush seems to have produced a lot more fruit!

An adorable but noisy lemur has taken an interest in the lab recently. The little animal loves attention and keeps chattering and squeaking at the researchers until they play with him. He's so cute that no one wants to chase him off, even though he is keeping them from working. They resign themselves to just accommodating him until he gets bored and moves on. Your villagers lose some tech points.

Today the villagers decide to celebrate mushrooms, in all their sizes, colors and deliciousness! Such industry from those little youngsters is indeed worthy of praise and glad celebration! There will be dancing and cake for the children.

Wasps have made their way through the brambles and started to make nests around the village. Unaware of the unwelcome visitors, the villagers continue playing and working nearby. Many villagers have been stung, and some of them are experiencing a bad reaction to the stings.

Today the villagers decide to celebrate collecting their 500th mushroom. Such industry from those little youngsters is indeed worthy of praise and glad celebration! There will be dancing and cake for the children.
A large barrel full of giggling infants comes bobbing down the stream. For some reason, nobody acts particularly surprised. They are happily adopted.
A large barrel full of giggling infants comes bobbing down the stream. For some reason, these babies prefer the Isolans and are adopted by them.

A freak wind has come up, filling the air with salt-laden sand, apparently from some nearby salt flat. The salty dust is stifling and burns the villagers' eyes, and they all have to hide until things settle down.
The Canoe from the Other Side
A canoe has just landed on the beach, piloted by a villager from another part of Isola.

Sitting alone one afternoon, {name} sees someone standing alone at the edge of the forest. Approaching this stranger, {he/she} is filled with warmth and euphoria. Upon reaching the edge of the forest, it turns out that the stranger was just a trick of the light, but {name} is sure it meant more than this. {name} gains trust!

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that a wealth of honeycombs have appeared, seemingly out of nowhere.\n \n Your village gains {award} food.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that someone or something has stolen some food.\n \n Your village has lost {award} food.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover a number of very useful scientific instruments that seem to have come out of nowhere, as though they simply fell from the sky.\n \n Your village has gained {award} tech points.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that someone or something has stolen some important research tools.\n \n Your village has lost {award} tech points.
Today is the day that the villagers pay their respects to those who have passed on.

Today is the day that the villagers give thanks to those that guide their fate and for all the blessings they enjoy on the island of Isola. There will be dancing and ceremonies, followed by a sumptuous feast!

One of the more meticulous farmers has just noticed that there are a whole bunch of berries growing way in the back, where they had been previously overlooked. It looks like there are quite a few more berries left than they thought!

The villagers hear a racket in the distance that sounds like a large drum rolling down a hill. A moment later, they see a barrel with little heads peeking out of it appear at the top of the highest waterfall. Horrified, they watch it plummet down the waterfalls until it reaches the pond where it slowly bobs about, and they manage to grab it before it sinks. Much to their relief, they find several giggling kids in the barrel, completely unharmed!

Some small children are heard giggling with glee, when to everyone's astonishment, a handful of toddlers shoot out of the bushes and splash into the hot springs! Still giggling, one of the children shouts: "Wanna do the slide again!" The villagers realize that it may take a very long time to find a way back to the children's village, because there are many treacherous features on Isola that isolate villages from one another. All they can do for now is take care of these children.
The villagers have been feeling glum and moody recently. Seeing the sacred tree in such a sorry state has had an adverse effect on their health and sense of well-being.

A respected master from another tribe has decided to join the expedition to this part of the island. {He/She} brings news that the fabled golden child from the south shore has gone missing. \n The newcomer is welcomed to the tribe.

A tame bird is found with a note tied to its leg. It bears news from another village saying that there are signs that the balance is starting to be restored to the island through the combined efforts of the other tribes. Scientific evidence follows... \n Your tribe gains some tech from the document.
The villagers have been very happy and ambitious lately. Encouraged and inspired by the improving health of the sacred tree, everyone seems to feel rejuvenated.

As the sun comes up, the tribe is greeted by desperate crying coming from the bushes. Several babies have been abandoned by someone, although they have been carefully swaddled to keep them warm and comfortable. Some of the tribe's women graciously volunteer to take care of the poor infants.
{name} woke up with lots of weird bites on {his/her} arm and thinks maybe bed bugs are infesting the huts.
Search for the bugs all night

{name} finds that {he/she} just cannot get back to sleep knowing that these biting pests are hiding somewhere in {his/her} bed. {He/She} turns the whole place inside out, fumigating with a smoldering piece of wood, until {he/she} is satisfied that it's safe to go back to sleep. Unfortunately, it is now dawn, and {he/she} is exhausted.

{name} is not happy about the bug infestation, but {he/she} is too tired to do anything about it now. {name} decides to go back to sleep. In the morning, {he/she} is covered with itchy and mildly infected bites. The tribe decides that this infestation must be dealt with and thoroughly fumigates the village with herbal smoke.
{name} has found one of the Native Isolans' masks on the ground.

{name} puts the mask on to see what it feels like. The moment {he/she} puts it on, {he/she} sees visions of fire and sorrow. "What was that?!" {name} exclaims. "Was I thinking that? Or was it magic...?" {name} quickly takes the mask off and places it back where it was. {name} ponders over the meaning of what {he/she} saw. {He/She}'s not sure where the visions came from, but something tells them that it was not something to ignore. "It reminds me of the stories of my grandparents... They always said our ancestors survived a terrible disaster, and lost a lot as a result. What happened to them must have been horrible... I wonder if the Isolans wear masks because something bad happened to them, too." After some reflection, {name} decides to live amongst the Isolans for a while in an attempt to understand them better.

{name} wonders what happened to the mask's owner. Did they lose it, or did they decide to take it off? Either way, {he/she} believes it's wrong to touch someone else's property without permission. {He/She} wishes the mask's owner well and carries on their way. {name} feels good having done the right thing, and learns to respect others better. {name} gains trust. Isola gains Life Energy.
One day while playing, little {name} finds an unusual toy. On closer examination {he/she} is fairly certain that {he/she} saw a child from the Isolan Tribe playing with it before.

Though it probably wasn't the right thing to do, little {name} keeps the toy and is able to glean some insight into the ways of the Native Isolans - at least the ways of the tribe's children. \n {name} gains research skill.

{name} decides to return the toy to the child that {he/she} believes to be the toy's rightful owner. The child was obviously looking for the lost toy and is very happy to get it back. The two play together for a while, and {name} feels good for having made a friend and for the knowledge of having acted in accordance with the best traditions of {his/her} people. \n {name} gains devotion skill, and {his/her} trust is strengthened.
{name} decides that it might be fun to try jumping off the bridge, tethered by stretchy vines, in pursuit of a new thrill!
What a ride! That was fun! {name} becomes obsessed with mastering the "stretchy-vine jump" and forgets about all of {his/her} other ambitions and obligations.
Late one night, {name} spots a mysterious figure working in the lab...

"Hello. My name is Biggles. Nice to meet you! Alas, I'm afraid you've seen too much." Biggles smiles and raises a jeweled talisman. There is a flash of light. When {name} wakes up, {he/she} can't seem to remember anything, even {his/her} own name! Oddly, {name} seems to have somehow gained uncanny insights into matters of science.

Using ordinary equipment from the lab, the man performs a number of miraculous procedures far beyond the villager's knowledge. He knows he's being watched, and, without turning around, he says, "My name is Biggles. I am here to correct certain errors. You'll thank me later!" He puts some glowing objects in his pockets and vanishes in a blinding light. He has left behind some of his amazing improvised devices. \n \n Your village gains {award} tech points.

Although normally occupied by the Isolans, {name} finds the hot springs empty one morning. {He/She} takes the opportunity to relax and close their eyes for a bit. Some time later, {he/she} wakes up to the sound of drumming and splashing, and is irritated by the Isolans' rude awakening. Suddenly they all stop and stare at {him/her}.

{name} looks around and sees many ceremonial implements and decorations. {name} realizes that {he/she} has overstayed their visit and that {he/she} has accidentally interrupted an important ceremony. {He/She} quickly exits the pools and apologizes for {his/her} intrusion, which the Isolans thankfully accept. The elders give a firm warning about the sanctity of the springs and tell {name} not to intrude again. {He/She} promises to be more respectful of their traditions. Both sides share a blessing of peace and go on their way.

{name} is rejuvenated by the warm, bubbly water in the pools. {He/She} says to the Isolans, "Who are you to hog up these lovely baths? You're ruining the atmosphere. Go do your frolicking somewhere else!" The Isolans are shocked at {name}'s statement and respond, "Intruder! You have trespassed on our holy springs and desecrated the sanctity of this ceremony. Now, you will pay for your mockery." {name} hides {his/her} face in fear, but by the time the crowd disperses, {name} is captured and interrogated for their crime. Full of regret at their foolishness, {name} decides to make up for it by working for the Isolans.
{name} decides that if {he/she} cannot see this "Guiding Hand", maybe it does not actually exist. {He/She} looks up and demands a sign right this minute!

Out of nowhere, hundreds of butterflies circle {name}. Already filled with doubt, however, {name} is unconvinced and believes there is a natural explanation for this phenomenon. Faith must come from within.

Faith must come from within, and a doubter will not be convinced this way. Eventually, {name} overcomes {his/her} doubt, though. {He/She} becomes one of the more outspoken believers that someone is guiding events on the island.

Little {name} becomes curious about the masked people and stakes out a secret spot from which to observe them more closely. After nearly an hour, {he/she} gets caught by one of the warriors, whose eyes appear hardened and scary.

Little {name} barely manages to get away. {He/She} did manage to figure out some things about these mysterious, masked people before {he/she} had to flee, however. From what they saw, they looked very sad and afraid of something. {name} feels bad for them, and wants to help them somehow. Perhaps this knowledge will come in handy in the future.

{name} has become fascinated by the Isolans' scientific advancement and prowess. {He/She} would like to observe their experiments in-person, as it seems they're about to reach a groundbreaking step in their latest discovery. As an aspiring scientist, {name} knows that new research is untested and carries a risk of danger, but is not sure whether to attend or pass up on this rare opportunity for their own safety.

{name} is delighted by the progress made on this experiment. However, during a crucial and extremely precise technique, a sudden explosion happens, and everyone present has to evacuate the lab! {name}, along with the other scientists, is left shaken and injured, but overall, has no hard feelings. This is all just part of research and development, after all!

{name} is delighted by the progress made on this experiment. {He/She} has learned a lot about the Isolans' way of thinking and was able to share {his/her} own ideas with the greater scientific community. {name} has made a lot of wonderful connections and is feeling ecstatic at the possibility of collaborating with the Isolans on new research projects in the future!

{name} decides that the lab is too crowded right now and being there would only be a nuisance. Anyway, it's none of {his/her} business to interfere with others' experiments. {name} decides it might be best to leave them alone.

One of the villagers notices that little {name} is missing and thinks one of the Isolans must be responsible for kidnapping them. One of the adults confronts an Isolan regarding little {name}. The Isolan seems very upset and angry at the accusation.
Try to talk to the Isolan

Your villagers come to the rescue and chase off the Isolan. The villagers lose their opportunity to question the alleged kidnapper about little {name}, but {he/she} is found days later with another child from the Isola Tribe, both having caught colds from having been lost outside these last few days in the jungle. Some of your villagers feel bad for falsely accusing an innocent person for kidnapping one of their children, and go off to apologize.

The villager and the Isolan talk for a while, and realize that their children may have gone off somewhere together. They share information about the children's favorite spots and quickly find them in the jungle. Both adults are grateful that their children are safe, and thank each other for helping out.

Offering a tour, the envoy is delighted to see how well-off the villagers are and offers a tour in return. It is most enlightening to the villagers, and each tribe learns something interesting about the other's culture and beliefs. The members of the village's expedition team agree to a trade deal with the Isolan envoy, and exchange some useful artifacts, knowledge and food items. Could this be the first step towards an understanding?
The Isolan envoy is disappointed, but leaves in peace.

{name} has been investigating certain sites in this new part of the island and believes that one of these sites may have been an important center of the Isolans' civilization. Today, {he/she} has found some amazing artifacts to support {his/her} theory.

{name} prepares a presentation based on {his/her} independent research. The findings are well received by the scientific community at large. Many believe that these findings will lead to whole new avenues of research. \n Your tribe gains a level in science.

Unfortunately, the research is not well received. The villagers find several flaws in {name}'s hypothesis, and raise a lot of questions about {his/her} methodology of study. {name} is flustered and unable to defend {himself/herself} against the tirade of questions. The senior scientists advise {him/her} to start from scratch and reformulate {his/her} entire experiment. {name} is very disappointed and decides that {he/she} may not be cut out to be a scientist after all.

{name} decides that {he/she} will need the help of the other researchers to properly conduct {his/her} investigation into these mysterious objects. The research is difficult, but gradually the objects begin to give up their ancient secrets.

{name} has discovered that the Isolans have some important scrolls stored in their lab supplies. They don't seem to be using them, but {name} believes that these scrolls might have some useful information that could help {him/her} overcome a particularly difficult research problem. {name} thinks that {he/she} could either try to negotiate a trade or perhaps {he/she} could "borrow" them, with the proper distraction.
Trade some food for the scrolls

Against {his/her} better judgement, {name} crafts a large smoke bomb instead of focusing on their research. At midnight, {name} deploys the smoke bomb and sneaks into the Isolans' camp to steal the scrolls. The next morning, rumors of a theft spread around both villages, triggering fights and distrust among the people. {name} tries to use the scrolls' knowledge in {his/her} research but is unable to find a solution. Looking at the scrolls again, {name} discovers that there is a piece missing and is mortified at what {he/she}'s done. Realizing {his/her} mistake, {he/she} sheepishly returns the scrolls and confesses in the middle of the conflict. Everyone is disappointed at {name}'s deceit, but is grateful for {his/her} honesty. {name} is ashamed of {his/her} actions and vows to work harder from now on.\n Your tribe gains 1500 tech points.

{name} arranges a barter session with an envoy from the Isolans' village. Finally, they agree to trade the scrolls for 100 food. The trade goes smoothly, and {name} gains some respect from the Isolans for {his/her} honest business practices. Also, one of the Isolan scientists reveals a missing piece that they had kept for safekeeping! Good thing they mentioned it! \n Your tribe gains 3000 tech points.

Fruit bats have come to inhabit the nearby trees as a stop in their migration. They could either be scared away, to prevent them from eating up the fruit, or observed to see if anything can be learned from them.

{name} decides to just sit and quietly observe the bats. After a while {he/she} realizes that plants and grasses are growing quite rapidly under the trees where they roost. Their droppings must be an excellent fertilizer. {name} realizes that this could be the key to raising sustainable crops! Unfortunately the bats have devoured all of the noni fruit in the process. \n Your tribe gains a level of farming tech.
{name} has little patience for freeloading bats, who are devouring their fruit! {He/She} gathers the tribe to drive them off!
Small juice-sucking bugs are literally sucking the life out of the crops! Something must be done, but this must be handled wisely, because they could become a chronic problem.

After some study, the villagers figure out that there are small creatures that live in certain types of soil that will eat the aphids' eggs before they hatch. This process is not immediate, but it's effective and long lasting. \n {name} gains farming expertise. \n Your village gains tech points.
The villagers decide to try using a potion to destroy the pests outright. While it is completely and immediately effective, it also destroys most of the plants!

One of the Isolans approaches your villagers, saying they wish to understand the tribe better. They speak of fear and confusion between their people, and hope that living together might help bridge the divide. {He/She} seems very sincere, but some of the villagers are a little suspicious, because this petitioner can't have come to understand much about their ways or culture in such a short time. Should they welcome the stranger into their tribe or politely send {him/her} back to {his/her} people?

At first, {name} is quiet and uneasy. The villagers, too, struggle to know what to say or do. But little by little, through small acts of kindness and patience on both sides, fear begins to fade. Eventually, {name} comes out of {his/her} shell and becomes a valued part of the community.

Despite their best efforts to help, nerves and miscommunication lead to an accident that damages important tools. Embarrassed and afraid of causing more trouble, {name} quietly returns to {his/her} people. The villagers feel regret, realizing how fragile new trust can be. Your tribe loses 2,000 tech points.

The villagers politely explain that this is a big decision, and {name} should probably take some time to understand their culture before so profoundly changing the course of {his/her} life. "The door will still be open for you later if you still want to join us later," they tell {him/her}. {name} seems to understand the wisdom of this advice and returns to {his/her} people in peace.
{name} has found a strange bowl woven of reeds. {He/She} thinks it could be either a hat or some kind of strainer to boil grains in.
Use it as a cooking strainer

The bowl works splendidly as a strainer for their traditional method of preparing wild grains. Unfortunately, it doesn't last long, because it was, in fact, a straw hat and never meant for this purpose. So, it turns out to be a short-term boon, but a boon nonetheless.
One day, {name} finds a very unusual blossom on a strange plant that no one has ever seen in bloom before. At the bottom of the cup-like blossom is an irresistibly sweet smelling nectar.
{name} takes a sip of the nectar and quickly feels rejuvenated! Moreover {he/she} feels incredibly energetic! Has everyone else just slowed down?

It's better to not mess with consuming random things without thorough research. The sample is brought back to the other researchers for further study, which yields encouraging results. \n Your tribe gains 2000 tech points.

One of the Isolans has a sack on their head instead of their mask and seems very distraught. On a nearby rock lies a wooden mask broken in two. {name} knows that a simple glue can easily be made from noni sap and sand, but this Isolan seems too upset to remember how. {name} wonders whether to help the Isolan fix the mask, or tell them to let it go, as it's broken, and they can always get a new one.\n What should {name} do?
Tell them to let it go

{name} approaches the Isolan and starts speaking, but the Isolan is startled by {his/her} sudden appearance and hits {him/her} in self-defense. Once they realize {name}'s true intentions, they apologize and gladly accept {his/her} help. While working together, the Isolan explains that the masks provide protection and safety and are deeply cherished by their people. "These masks are priceless. They are unique, just like we are. Whenever we feel betrayed by the world, they remind us that we're resilient and strong. There are others like us, who understand what we've gone through, and that we belong in this world." {name} recalls the stories of their ancestors, who experienced similar struggles of their own after surviving the destruction of their home. "Really? So you know what it's like? That's... good to know..." the Isolan says quietly. {name} observes the Isolan's eyes tear up as they carefully fit the broken halves of the mask back together. {He/She} senses that this act of kindness healed more than just the Isolan's mask. Something deep within their heart began to heal, too. Though slightly injured, {name} realizes that their peoples have more in common than they thought. {name} appears to have made a friend and gained valuable experience in treating others with tact and empathy.

The Isolan is devastated by {name}'s careless words, and cries that this mask is the only thing they had left to protect themself. "Now I've got nothing! Nothing!" The Isolan, feeling vulnerable and defenseless, yells for help. {name} is taken aback by the Isolan's emotional distress, not fully grasping the depth of their fear. The commotion causes other members of their tribe to rush over and defend their friend. Believing {name} to be an enemy, they quickly overwhelm and capture {name}, forcing {him/her} to answer to their Chief.
Little {name} has discovered a vial filled with a weird liquid that smells strongly of some combination of cheese and peppermint.

{name} swallows the strange liquid, gagging as it goes down. "I probably should not have drunk that," {he/she} thinks to {himself/herself}. A few hours later, {name} starts noticing all the subtle aromas of the world that {he/she} never really noticed before. {He/She} can even smell mushrooms from far away. {name} really loves mushrooms and begins putting {his/her} newly extra-sensitive nose to work finding every last mushroom hidden in this part of the island. Unfortunately, as a side effect, {name} is overly sensitive to strong odors and, therefore, has trouble with any kind of work other than farming. \n Your tribe gains food.
{name} has heard about strange, magical vials, and this one smells terrible. {He/She} would have to be crazy to drink this one!
{name} found a vial with an irresistible, floral-smelling liquid inside.
You shouldn't drink strange liquids. You might shrink or turn into a baby or something!

One day, {name} steps on something that hurts {his/her} foot. What can this be? It's invisible! By feeling it, {name} figures out that it's a small vial and believes that this one, being invisible, must contain a potion of great power. For days, {he/she} agonizes over the decision of whether or not to sample its mysterious contents.

{name} finally decides to drink the contents and is surprised that it only contains a tiny sip of berry juice. Also, quite surprisingly, it refills itself, this time with honey water. {name} puzzles over this for a time and finally realizes that the vial is a lesson: Don't be afraid of the unknown, because having the courage to explore it often yields a sweet surprise! {name} takes this lesson to heart and becomes curious about the true nature of all things.
{name} does not think it is worth the risk. Any possible benefit would never make up for all the pain and trouble of ingesting a potentially toxic substance. Better just to forget it.

{name} believes that the fruit would cook faster in the cooking pit if {he/she} was balanced on top of the covered fruit, applying constant pressure while it cooks. This is obviously extremely dangerous, but could it work?

{name} sets the fruit under a banana leaf and begins to balance on the hard round bump. In a few moments the fruit begins to soften, and {name} quickly hops off and retrieves the cooked fruit! It is very effective and {name} is setting the bar among farmers!

{name} sets the fruit under a banana leaf and prepares to step onto the fruit. Even before {his/her} foot reaches the covered fruit, {he/she} slips and stumbles into the hot coals! That was a bad idea...
{name} knows better than to try this kind of crazy thing. Those coals are hot and very unforgiving.

One evening, {name} encounters a mysterious stranger. Ordinarily, {name} would just run away, but there is something familiar about this stranger... something from the stories of the older parts of the island. The stranger instructs {name} to gather the other children for an important lesson.
Run away and tell the adults

{name} decides that this is a matter that must be handled by the adults. {He/She} runs home and wakes the adults, who immediately form a search party to find the mysterious and creepy intruder. However, by the time they arrive, he is gone. All that remains is a strange cloud of luminous smoke.

The mysterious stranger gazes across his audience and announces, "Fear not! It is only me, Biggles! Perhaps you have heard of me? Yes? No? I have an important lesson for you clever children. When people suffer loss, sometimes the pain stirs them to action. Those who learn from it will grow in courage, while those who run will be bound by its weight. Only through acceptance and understanding can the darkness turn to light. You know, there are others on this island. Others who are much like you. Others who, for a very long time, have tried their hardest to survive against adversity. They have lived secluded, burdened by memories they could not face. Their hearts are clouded, afraid to take steps towards healing. Only when all hearts are in balance can the island be restored." With these words the man vanishes, leaving only a cloud of luminous smoke. What could this mean?

{name} hears crying and finds a village child stuck high up on a branch in the great Tree of Life. No amount of coaxing will bring {him/her} down. It will be very dangerous for an adult to climb that high on the tree and help the child down. Perhaps the child should be left to have a lesson about consequences.

{name} climbs up the tree and helps the child find a path back down through the branches. Predictably, {name}'s own descent does not go so smoothly. The second branch {he/she} touches snaps loudly! {name} tumbles down through the branches and hit the ground hard. Oh well. Parenting requires sacrifices.

Children have to learn about the consequences of their actions. {name} leaves the child. Hours later the small, subdued youth returns to the village, bruised and angry. It is not obvious whether it was a lesson about consequences or just a lesson about falling down.

Two children have been constantly fighting over a pretty, round shell.{name} is sick of the bickering and decides to intervene. The children will have to either be taught to share the shell, or they will have to decide who will keep it.
Sharing is important and teaching children about this is good parenting. They agree to share the shell, and {name} reflects on how well this went.

Not everything can be shared, and in this case a lesson about negotiation is more valuable. However, even after they pick an owner for the shell, one of the children feels very bad, outmatched at the debate over the shell. Still, the fighting has stopped. {name}'s approach was innovative and effective, although maybe a bit harsh.

{name} discovers a mysterious figure lurking by the tree one night. Sensing {name}, the figure turns, smiles and says: "Hello, my child. My name is Biggles. Perhaps you have heard of me? I have been watching you. Your people have done well in returning the balance to Isola. I will tell you something: The island, like life, is a wheel. This tree you see here is its axle. To restore balance the axle must be true. Now, because your people are worthy, I will answer one question:"
How should we care for our people?
How should we care for the tree?

"Yes, I see that you are a good and caring people. I will teach you a secret." Biggles teaches {name} some advanced and arcane medical knowledge When {name} turns to thank him, he is simply not there! Where could he have gone?

"Yes, I see that you are a good and wise people. I will teach you a secret." Biggles teaches {name} some advanced and arcane techniques in dendrology. When {name} turns to thank him, he is simply not there! Where could he have gone?
